about: HOW THE TRAINER TRAINS: its own settings and its own rules, as data. The trainers read this and nothing of it is written into their code, so the way a swarm is trained can be changed, by a person or by the trainer itself, without changing a program. Each configuration keeps its own changes to it (training/states/), made by the review step from what a pass measured, each with its reason.

keep.about: A change is kept only if, question by question on the same train questions, it wins this many more answers than it loses, and does no worse on the held ones.

trials.about: How many arrangements a pass tries one change from here, how many that are several changes from here at once (wild) and how many changes each of those is (depth), and whether a trial stops once it can no longer be kept.

moves.about: How much each kind of move counts for when the plan ranks what to try.

review.about: When a pass looks at itself, and the rules it applies. A rule: when a number it measured passes a mark, change one setting, within bounds, and say why.

rules.why: The same arrangement measured twice differed by {metric} answers. A change must win by more than that to be kept.
The same arrangement measured twice gave the same answers. One answer won is a real gain.
On {metric%} of the questions no slot had the larger model's answer. Sending answers back and looping gives a draft another go: the order of steps counts for more.
On {metric%} of the questions a slot had the larger model's answer and the reply did not. What the decider is shown counts for more.
Nothing was kept for {metric} passes. More arrangements are tried each pass.
Nothing was kept for {metric} passes. One change at a time is not finding it: more arrangements that are several changes from here are tried.
Nothing was kept for {metric} passes. The arrangements tried at once are made further from this one.

ratchet.about: A bar that is held tightens: a kind of question the swarm has been at parity on, on the held questions, for this many passes in a row is asked more of (half as many again, each time, up to max times).
